extracted.intended_audience: contracting officers, administrative contracting officers (ACOs), Department of Defense procurement officials, and contractors performing DoD contracts
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance (Armed Services Procurement Regulation / ASPR amendments) governing acquisition, leasing, reporting, and contract clauses for automatic data processing equipment (ADPE), contractor team arrangements, use of GSA supply sources, tax clause insertion, and related procurement procedures for DoD and other Federal contracting activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of ADPE section
rubrics_metrics.description: This section is applicable to all ADPE, as defined in § 1.201-29 of this chapter, except as components of end items to be delivered to the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADPE definition reference (§ 1.201-29) identifies scope; components of end items delivered to Government excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval required when ADPE is purchased or title passes
rubrics_metrics.description: If ADPE is purchased for the account of the Government or if title to the ADPE will pass to the Government, the acquisition must be approved as required by Part 13 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any purchase or transfer of title to Government requires Part 13 approval procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-approval review steps for leasing ADPE
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to approval of a proposed lease agreement (when total leasing cost will be reimbursed under cost-reimbursement contracts), the contracting officer shall: (1) Survey the Defense Supply Agency (DSAH-LSR) for availability of excess ADPE which could be issued as GFP and which would fulfill the contractor's requirements; (2) Determine whether leasing is the appropriate method under § 15.205-48; (3) Consider whether ADPE should be leased under a Federal Supply Schedule Contract; (4) If rental through a commercial contract is authorized, require a provision that the Government will have the initial option to utilize any purchase or other benefits earned through rental payments; (5) Obtain approval of the leasing arrangement from the Senior ADPE policy official of the Department/Agency which predominantly generated the requirement (for noncompetitive leases, forward request to Assistant Secretary of Defense (Installations and Logistics)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These five mandated pre-approval considerations must be documented and followed before approving leases whose cost will be reimbursed to contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for ACO arranged ADPE reviews and required submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the total cost of leasing ADPE in a single plant, division, or cost center exceeds $500,000 per year and 50 percent or more of the total cost is to be allocated to cost-reimbursement type contracts, the ACO should arrange for: (1) An initial review and an annual review thereafter of the contractor's ADPE system to evaluate existing capability and need to continue leasing; and (2) Submission by the contractor of any proposed lease of a new system and any proposed major changes to an existing system for advance determination of validity and reasonableness of leasing and resulting cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'major change' is defined as any addition or substitution of ADPE which will have an annual cost in excess of $25,000. Reviews are to support determination under § 15.205-48.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACO action after reviews (concurrence or nonconcurrence)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the initial and subsequent reviews, and after review of any proposed lease of a new system or major change, the ACO should either enter into an advance understanding with the contractor (see § 15.107) to provide a basis for concurrence in the proposed lease, or notify the contractor of the Government's nonconcurrence and of consequent cost disallowance contemplated under § 15.205-48.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use § 15.107 as basis for concurrence; nonconcurrence may lead to cost disallowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of technical ADP assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical ADP assistance will be provided as necessary to the contracting officer by the Department having the preponderance of interest with the contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting officers should request technical assistance from the responsible Department when implementing ADPE procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of title to low-cost equipment to nonprofit educational or research institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts with nonprofit institutions shall provide (or be amended to provide) for transfer to contractors of title to each item of equipment having an acquisition cost of less than $200 and purchased with funds available for grants or contracts for basic or applied research. For equipment already in possession, contracting officer shall vest in contractor title at amendment or as soon as practicable; for equipment acquired for the account of the Government, vest title upon receiving a written receipt from contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not applicable to transfers precluded by controls governing the equipment involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of contractor team arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: A contractor team arrangement is one whereby two or more companies form a partnership or joint venture to act as a potential prime contractor or whereby a potential prime contractor agrees with one or more other companies to act as his subcontractor(s) under a specified Government procurement or program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the official definition used to determine responsibilities and contractual structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on contractor team arrangements and Government reservation of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government will recognize the integrity and validity of contractor team arrangements provided they are identified and company relationships are stated in a proposal. Under a contractor team arrangement, the prime contractor is fully responsible for performance. The Government normally will not require dissolution of team arrangements. These policies do not authorize arrangements violating antitrust statutes and do not limit the Government's rights to: (1) Approve subcontracts in accordance with ASPR requirements; (2) Determine the responsibility of a prime contractor on the basis of the stated team arrangement; (3) Provide the selected prime contractor with data rights owned or controlled by the Government; (4) Pursue policies on competitive procurement, subcontracting and component breakout, after initial production procurement or at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prime remains fully responsible; Government retains oversight and procurement policy rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on contractors' use of GSA supply sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors shall not be authorized to utilize General Services Administration (GSA) supply sources (a) in connection with the performance of fixed-price type contracts, even though such contracts provide for price adjustment, escalation, redetermination, or cost-reduction incentive; or (b) for the leasing of equipment to be utilized in the performance of cost-reimbursement type contracts, other than ADPE for use only in performance of cost-reimbursement contracts where the entire rental cost will be charged to those contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors may use GSA supply source listings for price information; GSA catalogs/Federal Supply Contracts may be made available for review but not for direct use in forbidden situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic authority conditions for use of GSA supply sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors shall be authorized to utilize GSA supply sources only where: (a) title to property ordered under Federal Supply Schedule contracts will pass to and vest in the Government directly from the Federal Supply Schedule contractor; (b) the contractor will lease ADPE under a Federal Supply Schedule contract for use only in performance of cost-reimbursement contracts, and the entire rental cost will be charged to those contracts; or (c) where title to Government-owned property ordered from GSA stores stock will remain in the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three conditions define when GSA source usage is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insertion of commercial warranty and material inspection clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with § 1.324-4 of this chapter, an appropriate commercial warranty clause may be inserted. Material Inspection and Receiving Report clause is added per Defense Procurement Circular 54 of June 26, 1967—Item 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert appropriate warranty and inspection clauses per cited ASPR authorities; follow referenced circulars for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Davis-Bacon predetermination and publication of prevailing rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon determination that the Davis-Bacon Act is applicable to any item of work, the Contractor shall submit a request for a predetermination of the prevailing wage rates. Upon receipt, the Contracting Officer shall obtain a predetermination of applicable rates and publish such rates and incidental instructions in numbered attachments to the contract. Such attachments shall be considered the wage determination decision of the Secretary of Labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachments will indicate the work the rates apply to and the period within which subcontracts subject to such rates may be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of Government liability clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract clause limits: (a) the Contractor is not authorized to make expenditures or incur obligations in performance of this contract which exceed $____; (b) the maximum amount for which the Government shall be liable if this contract is terminated is $____.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values to be filled in per contract; clause caps contractor-authorized expenditures and Government termination liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payments clause for letter contracts (allowable costs prior to definitization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include 'Payments of Allowable Costs Prior to Definitization' clause in letter contracts contemplating a cost-type contract; allowable items of cost shall be determined by the Contracting Officer in accordance with the statement of cost principles set forth in Part ___ of Section XV of the ASPR. Reimbursement under this paragraph shall not exceed ___ percent of the maximum amount of Government liability otherwise set forth in the letter contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement clause with appropriate title, risk of loss, and other provisions; see §§163.72 and 163.74 for progress payment policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary conditions clause and remedies for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government shall notify the Contractor in writing of any failure to meet the sanitary standards prescribed by the contract. If not corrected within three (3) days of receipt of notice, the whole or part of the contract may be terminated for default or the Contractor's right to perform may be suspended for not less than ten (10) days. Suspension will not extend the life of the contract nor be sufficient cause to extend delivery time. During suspension, Government may procure from other sources and Contractor shall be liable for excess costs. If Contractor does not correct failures within any suspension period specified, the Government may terminate the unexpired portion of the contract for default without allowing additional time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-day correction window; ten-day minimum suspension; Government remedies include termination and procurement from other sources with contractor liability for excess costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADPE screening and reporting procedures (SF 120 reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government-owned ADPE or leased ADPE with options/residual interests will be reported to the Defense Supply Agency, DSAH-LSR, on Standard Form 120, 'Report of Excess Personal Property' (original and four copies). Normally acquisition studies permit projecting anticipated release date 180 days before equipment is available; ADPE should be reported as soon as possible, but the following minimum schedule applies: (1) Government-owned ADPE reported upon receipt of notice of complete termination or when determined property no longer needed; release date assigned will be last day of plant clearance period or 90 days after property becomes inactive (revised reports if release date changes). (2) Leased ADPE charged to cost-reimbursement contracts reported when determined property will no longer be needed or a major portion thereof; release date shall not extend rental beyond date it can be released to lessor. Prompt reporting is necessary to reutilize property and protect Government equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow SF 120 submission procedures and update release dates when necessary; ensure leased equipment release dates do not extend rental unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request and attachment of lessor quotation for leased ADPE
rubrics_metrics.description: For leased equipment the total cost of which is charged to one or more cost-reimbursement contracts, a quotation shall be requested from the lessor projecting the reduced price at which the equipment may be purchased based on accumulated rental credits through the anticipated release date. A copy of this quotation should be attached to the Standard Form 120, but submission of the SF 120 should not be delayed pending receipt of this information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain lessor projection of purchase price from rental credits and attach to SF 120 when available; do not delay reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required information to be reported on Standard Form 120
rubrics_metrics.description: SF 120 shall include: (1) A complete list of each equipment item identified by manufacturer's series and model number, modifications and attachments, identification number if Government-owned; indicate type of maintenance contract, contractor, and monthly cost. (2) A separate attachment showing time in service for each component, average utilization (hours per month) and average down-time per month for the 12-month period immediately preceding the report (and narrative of repeated equipment failure if appropriate). (3) A list of compilers and other software packages, engineering drawings and maintenance manuals available with the equipment. (4) For complete equipment configurations, information regarding power and air conditioning requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed technical, maintenance, utilization and support-software documentation to facilitate reutilization decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense Supply Agency control of reported excess ADPE
rubrics_metrics.description: The Defense Supply Agency shall control ADPE reported excess. Shipments shall be made upon receipt of requests approved by DSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DSA centrally controls disposition of reported excess ADPE and approves shipment requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: N.C. Sales and Use Tax clause insertion and refund entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: A provision of the N.C. Sales and Use Tax Act authorizes counties and incorporated cities/towns in North Carolina to obtain each year from the Commissioner of Revenue a refund of sales and use taxes indirectly paid on building materials, supplies, fixtures, and equipment which become part of or are annexed to any building or structure. United States is entitled to such benefit but must resort to refund procedure; to assure refunds the clause set forth shall be inserted in all construction contracts performed in North Carolina, including vessel repair contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert required clause in all NC construction contracts to enable Federal refund claims; follow State refund procedures and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for substantiating N.C. tax refund claims (contractor certified statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: To substantiate a refund claim, the claimant must secure from the contractor certified statements setting forth the cost of property purchased from each vendor and the amount of sales and/or use taxes paid thereon. If the contractor makes several purchases from the same vendor, the statement must indicate invoice numbers, inclusive dates of the invoices, total amount of invoices and sales/use taxes paid. The statement must also include cost of tangible personal property withdrawn from contractor's warehouse stock and taxes paid thereon. Similar certified statements by subcontractors must be obtained and furnished to the claimant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified vendor- and invoice-level detail is required; subcontractor statements are mandatory for refund substantiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and responsibilities for submission of certified N.C. tax statements and refund application
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction contractors must submit to contracting officers by August 31 each year certified statements covering N.C. sales and use taxes paid during the 12-month period ended the preceding June 30. Contracting officers must assure contractor compliance and obtain annual refund of N.C. sales and use taxes to which their activity may be entitled. The application for refund must be filed each year before December 31 in the manner and form required by the Commissioner of Revenue. If contract is completed before next July 1, certified statements shall be submitted within 60 days after completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First refund application will cover taxes paid July 1, 1966 to June 30, 1967; contracting officers are responsible for timely filing and compliance enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: N.C. Sales and Use Tax clause provisions and contractor certification form
rubrics_metrics.description: The clause (N.C. Sales and Use Tax (October 1966)) defines 'materials', treats N.C. taxes as included in fixed-price contract price or allowable cost in cost-reimbursement contracts, requires furnishing certified statements and subcontractor statements at specified times, and prescribes the certification wording to be furnished (sample form text provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the clause paragraphs (a)-(e) as to definition, tax treatment, certification timing, form content, and special ship-repair modification.
